title: Hybrid streaming requant kernel for low-overhead KV prefill and decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On INT8/FP8 inference paths we see disproportionate CPU/GPU time consumed by dequant/requant operations when building and streaming KV cache during long prefill phases. This is especially visible for long-context LLMs with mixed prefill/decode scheduling (prefill-heavy requests interleaved with short decode bursts), where repeated dequant loops and non-fused attention kernels add ~12-28% token latency and memory bandwidth pressure.

Goal: Implement a hybrid 'streaming requant' kernel plus a dynamic kernel selector that: 1) stores KV shards in compact scaled format (block-level scales), 2) performs on-the-fly fused attention + requant operations to avoid full-width dequant->compute->requant cycles, and 3) selects the fused vs. fallback kernel based on sequence length, batch shape, and current SLO headroom. This should reduce per-token dequant overhead and memory traffic while keeping numerical drift below our regression thresholds for quality monitoring.

Scope: runtime kernel work (CUDA + ROCm), kernel selector heuristics, integration with KV cache layout, unit and integration tests, benchmarking harness updates, and a canary rollout plan tied to runtime-1.20.

Success metrics: - 15-30% median token latency reduction on INT8/FP8 for prefill-dominant workloads, - <=0.5% perplexity change on held-out eval prompts, - no increase in memory footprint beyond 3% for typical batch profiles.

Notes: This is different from prior fused attention optimizations because we target the quantization boundary: minimizing explicit float dequant cycles and exploiting block-level scales to permit compute in mixed precision with occasional higher-precision accumulators.
